records.summary: This building is close to the Mevlana museum, it suddenly sprang up between visits I made in 2008 and 2010. It has a semi-classical appearance, and inside one can walk along diorama's showing several wars as well as peacefull living in a village. It was built in Seljuk-style to commemorate those who feell during the Cyprus Peace Operation, the Korean War and the War of Independence. The diorama's refer to the Çanakkale Wars and the War of Independence, the 30 August victory and show a village in Konya during the post-war recovery period. These pictures show the war, I think the ones where one can see a glimpse of the sea are the Çanakkale Wars ones, others will be of the War of Independence.

records.title: Military cemetery from World War I and World War II in Dąbrowa Tarnawacka near Tarnawatka (6).jpg
records.originalTitle: Military cemetery from World War I and World War II in Dąbrowa Tarnawacka near Tarnawatka (6).jpg
records.summary: Military cemetery in Dąbrowa Tarnawacka, located on the main road Zamość - Tomaszów Lubelski, at the edge of the forest, leaving Tarnawatka-Tartak towards Tomaszów Lubelski. The cemetery was established after 1915. The soldiers who died during the First World War are buried in this cemetery. A mound was made on top of the graves, topped with a cross. The cemetery was entered in the register of monuments. In 1939, soldiers from the first battle for Tomaszów Lubelski, who died on September 17-20, 1939, were buried here. The number of buried soldiers is unknown. It is estimated that it is about 300 people. They are soldiers and officers, mostly from the 73rd Katowice Infantry Regiment and units cooperating with it, including the 23rd Light Artillery Regiment under the command of Lt. Col. Władysław Ryłko. These units were part of the Silesian 23rd Infantry Division commanded by Colonel Władysław Powierza. The commander of the 73rd Infantry Regiment was Lt. Col. Piotr Sosialuk. The commander of the 23rd light artillery regiment was Lt. Col. Władysław Ryłko. On September 19 and 20, 1939, the Polish Army fought against Nazi Germany. Attacks were made from the forest in Zielone towards Szarowola. On the battlefield, among others, Commander of the 1st Battalion, Major Stanisław Woźniakowski, Commander of the 1st Company Captain Zygmunt Krasnopolski, and 2nd Lt. Jerzy Cott. The total losses were around 60%. On the left, next to the mass graves, there is a plaque with the inscription: "Graves of Polish soldiers who died in Dąbrowa Tomaszowska on September 20, 1939, in a battle with Germany, about 5 km from Tomaszów Lubelski". Honor their memory!

records.originalTitle: U.S.-China relations - communication and misperception in the Taiwan Strait (IA uschinrelationsc10945859).pdf
records.summary: Taiwan's political status remains the central, most difficult issue in U.S.-China relations. The question has created tensions that erupted in three crises of direct confrontation between the United States and China in the Taiwan Strait. The central dilemma in solving these conflicts has been that both states tied vital national interests to the issue. Despite the fact that both sides have managed to avoid the Taiwan question when negotiating agreements in less sensitive areas, Taiwan's status continues to present the greatest risk factor for a future armed conflict between the United States and China. This thesis examines the three Taiwan Strait crises and argues that experiential learning coupled with a realpolitik view of international relations has led decision-makers to follow consistent modes of behavior when handling them. The development of positive relations between the United States and China after 1971 has not mitigated the inherent risks presented by the Taiwan question. The thesis concludes that the value of strategic ambiguity is overestimated, given the likelihood of misperception by both parties in a mutual deterrence relationship. Since a future crisis may not be averted, the United States and China must develop robust lines of diplomatic communication to avoid inadvertent escalation. Subjects:

records.summary: This thesis assesses the potential of U.S. Naval Forward Presence in the Western Pacific to stabilize economic markets around the world in the event of a crisis in the South China Sea and the Taiwan Straits. It utilizes a scenario analogous to that of the 1995-96 Taiwan Strait crisis that it sets in the year 2005. The scenario utilizes existing military, political and economic conditions in the region to forecast likely behavior of the main actors. The thesis concludes that U.S. Naval Forward Presence is the vital ingredient to protect U.S. interests in the region, discourage crisis escalation, and stabilize world oil and financial markets.
